answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network roots agent identities in a curated trust garden, anchoring validation rights atop a verifiably staked knoll. When registering multiple synthetic peers, an attacker faces cryptographic stake burning where collateral requirements grow superlinearly as O(N^2). Each coordinated branch behaves like a connected vine, compounding burned stake across clustered identities and making large-scale proliferation cost-prohibitive.
